prompt: Do text message reminders improve on-time childhood vaccination?

sources.S1:
In a randomized trial at 14 clinics, parents who received text reminders completed their child's second measles dose on time at a rate of 78 percent, versus 71 percent for parents who did not get texts. The trial enrolled 6,200 families.

The effect was smaller among families who already had a regular pediatrician.
sources.S2: The texting service cost 0.40 dollars per family. The health department has not decided whether to expand it beyond the trial clinics.

writer.markdown:
# Question: Do text message reminders improve on-time childhood vaccination?

## Answer
Text reminders raised on-time second doses by 7 percentage points [S1]. On-time completion was 78 percent with texts and 71 percent without [S1]. Text reminders raised on-time completion to 87 percent [S1].

## Evidence
- Roughly 6,000 families took part in the trial [S1].
- Families were assigned to the two groups at random [S1].
- The effect was larger among families who already had a regular pediatrician [S1].
- Texting cost 40 cents per family [S2].
- Texting all 6,200 families cost about 2,480 dollars [S2].

## Counter-evidence and limits
- The department has decided to expand texting to every clinic in the state [S2].
- Families without a regular pediatrician saw a bigger effect [S1].
- Parents preferred texts over phone calls.

## Next actions
- Estimate the cost of a countywide rollout (judgment)

## Sources
- [S1] Randomized reminder trial
- [S2] Health department cost note
